summary: Medusa (Ancient Greek: Μέδουσα) in this atlas entry is a Mycenaean princess, daughter of King Sthenelus and Nicippe (Antibia / Archippe) daughter of Pelops, and sister of Eurystheus and Alcyone. She is not the Gorgon slain by Perseus.

sections.heading: Perseid princess
paragraphs: Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 2.4.5) names Medusa among Sthenelus' children by Nicippe beside Alcyone and Eurystheus. Some later notices call her Astymedusa and make her a second wife of Oedipus after Jocasta — a Theban marriage tradition, not Homeric.
In the atlas she is typed to the Mycenaean Perseid genealogy; no independent deed is recorded beyond kinship to the taskmaster king Eurystheus.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Never merge with the Gorgon Medusa (atlas medusa), nor with Medusa daughter of Priam, Medusa daughter of Pelias, or Medusa wife of Polybus of Corinth. The atlas id medusa-sthenelid is Sthenelus' daughter alone.
